summary: Heidi Fjeld works in Tibetology and other fields. She earned her Doctor Rerum Politicarum at the University of Oslo (circa 2001-2006) under Signe Howell and served there as a postdoctoral fellow circa 2007-2010.

Heidi I. Koppl is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Copenhagen under Christian K. Wedemeyer and also studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Sherab Zangpo.
Heidi Pauwels is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied at KU Leuven in 1983 and 1986 and earned her PhD at the University of Washington in 1994, where she held a post around 1996.

Heinrich Blochmann was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He pursued his studies at Leipzig University (circa 1855-1857) and the University of Calcutta (circa 1860-1862).

Heinrich Ewald was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and Indology. After studying at the Große Schule and under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn at the University of Göttingen, he held professorships at Göttingen (1824-1837, 1848-1867) and Tübingen (1838-1848).

Heinrich Hettrich was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saarland University (circa 1968-1974) and the University of Giessen (circa 1974-1979). He held posts at Munich (circa 1981-1985), Saarland (circa 1985-1989), and Würzburg (circa 1989-2012).

Heinrich Hübschmann was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Jena (circa 1868-1870) and under Martin Haug (circa 1870-1872), later holding a post at Leipzig University (circa 1876-1877).

Heinrich Kiepert was an archaeology and history scholar. He studied at the Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium and Frederick William University Berlin (1837), later holding posts at the Landes-Industrie-Comptoir zu Weimar (1845-1852) and Frederick William University Berlin (1859).
Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer specialized in linguistics and other fields. After studying at Leipzig University from circa 1819 to 1824, he held a post there from circa 1835 to 1888.

Heinrich Lüders was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He held posts at Oxford, Göttingen, Rostock, Kiel, and Humboldt University of Berlin (1909).
Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Bernhard Hirzel from circa 1836 to 1838. He held an academic post at the University of Zurich from circa 1849 to 1889.
Heinrich Uhle was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus from circa 1863 to 1867. He served as a professor at the Kreuzschule from circa 1872 to 1907.

Heinrich Wenzel was an Indologist and Tibetologist who studied at Jena, Tübingen, and Leipzig, and under Heinrich August Jäschke, Léon Feer, and Georg von der Gabelentz. He completed his Habilitation at Leipzig University in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Rudolf von Roth, Siegfried Goldschmidt, Ernst Windisch, Wilhelm Scherer, and Albrecht Weber. He held posts at Greifswald, Humboldt University of Berlin, Heidelberg, and Columbia.

Heinz Bechert was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at Saarland University (circa 1956-1964), the University of Göttingen (circa 1965-2000), and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (circa 1973-2005).

Heinz Mode was a scholar of archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studying under George Peiris Malalasekera, Otto Fischer, and at the University of Basel, he was Professor of Oriental Archaeology at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1948-1978).

Helen Hardacre specializes in religious studies and Japanology. She was a member of the Department of Religion at Princeton University (attested 1988-1996) and held a post at Harvard University circa 1990.

Helen J. Baroni is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt, later taking a post at the University of Hawaii around 1993.

Helena Blankleder is an active scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Her education includes studying under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, both attested in 1999.
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1979 to 1984. She held an academic post at Rice University circa 1990.
